body_text:
I hope you and your new team were able to get to know each other this past week, and were able to make good progress on your Team Charter at the help ID-EAF2D41E12054796. This week in tutorial you will start working, ID-6F07CECD2B398573 your team, on your ID-58D15EDA1C3A6CE1 ID-FF1B854C260B0B5E.
 The Team Charter assignment is slightly unique in that the deadline for this team assignment is the start of your Wtkt 21 Tutorial. Make sure your team has a plan to submit it on time. Buffer enough time to deal ID-6F07CECD2B398573 technical complications. (IE. Do not submit just two minutes before the deadline).
 Before your tutorial, review the Wtkt 21 Tutorial Agenda and the Preliminary ID-FF1B854C260B0B5E Worksheet (PPW) posted in the Wtkt 21 To Do of the ID-C72B665F897643CE Quercus modules. Note the individual ID-B98B0772F2A06715 that starts the agenda. Give some thought about the Gap-Need-Scope of the Pinecrest Courtyard ID-FF1B854C260B0B5E. Use what you wrote in your PS Adam as a foundation, Lakeshore building on it. Your PS Adam will NOT be returned to you before your tutorial, so you will need to go ID-67449CF44F7EA03C memory. The more prepared each team member is for this portion of the agenda the sooner the team will get their draft PPW completed.
 Your team must get your team-written PPW reviewed by your TA before the end of tutorial. Do not underestimate the importance of the PPW (Gap-Need-Scope). Like any ID-58D15EDA1C3A6CE1 ID-FF1B854C260B0B5E there is not just one set of these. Differences can lead the team in vastly different directions. Additionally a team that is not in agreement ID-6F07CECD2B398573 these foundational aspects will soon find themselves in conflict. Before the end of this tutorial make sure your team has one path forward and that everyone agrees on that path.
 Finally make sure you have a ID-FF1B854C260B0B5E Plan and a ID-B157AC51C4CC37F9 Plan to keep your team moving forward.
 Monday, ID-7A0B1043FF98B5CA ID-ED63F4E2D9C9EACD is Orange Shirt Day and the National Day of Truth and Reconciliation. This is a day to promote all Reconciliation initiatives, but especially to raise awareness for the survivors of the Residential School System. It is tradition on this day to wear an Orange Shirt. This shirt can be one sold by reputable sellers where the proceeds go towards charitable organizations supporting Indigenous causes. Last I heard there were still such shirts for sale at the Bookstore. However, you do not need one of these shirts. You can show your support for the cause by wearing ANY orange shirt.
 If this day is new to you, then you can read more about it here: https://resource-4d7035c72454ba04.example.edu
 As well, at the start of all MMF324 ID-A58ECBA3CB070DDA sections on Monday I’ll spend a few minutes discussing the meaning behind this day. If ID-941BF72D1E900F56 of the Residential School System is something you are not emotionally prepared to hear, please plan to arrive 5 minutes late. You will not be penalized for caring for your ID-97414BDC6DAB599D ID-433A517927D1969A on this day, which is emotionally draining for many.
 If you wear an orange shirt to MMF324 ID-A58ECBA3CB070DDA on Monday I will grant you one PD Point.

announcement_title: Final Grades
author: Kristy Campos
body_text:
Dear Students,
 Happy New Year! We hope your ID-35167F231ED84614 term is off to a great start, even if it does not feel like ID-35167F231ED84614 just yet.
 We are writing to let you know about some post final exam/final grades ID-4FC4C2142F6C73B9.
 Gerald I get to see my graded final exam?
 Yes. The Faculty has let us know that we may release your graded final exams and this will be done shortly after posting this announcement. As ID-6F07CECD2B398573 the term tests, you will be able to see the distribution of final exam grades in the email ID-67449CF44F7EA03C Gradescope (if you are interested in this sort of thing).
 Solutions to the Final Exam will not be posted.
 Were there any adjustments made to the final grades?
 Yes. Some adjustments (only positive ones) were made to the grades however ID-C72B665F897643CE grades were not (and are not, in general) “curved” in any direction to fit a particular distribution. The adjustments included re-weighting the universal make-up test (provided your universal make-up test grade was greater than both your Term Test I & II grades), and some rounding, where appropriate.
 There will not be any further adjustments. Please do not ask for any.
 How can I submit a regrade request for my final exam?
 Please see here: https://resource-c667d3ffdf6ff7f4.example.edu/pc02ec22a/pc17b7548/p9a18caaa
 At a minimum, please be aware of the following:
 1 . There are costs and deadlines involved in submitting a final exam regrade request. These are set by the Faculty, not us.
 2. Your final grade may increase, decrease, or stay the same as a result of a final exam regrade request.

announcement_title: Expectations for the Final Exam
author: Molly Branch
body_text:
Dear EMB222 Students,
 A practice final exam has been posted in the "Preston Serrano" module. Office hours in the weeks leading up to the exam will be posted shortly.
 We wanted give you some guidance for your studying for the final exam and our expectations for written answers and drawings/diagrams on the final exam.
 Written Justifications
 Some exam ID-493BD7E0444E440F say "Provide a well-written justification". A well written justification is a justification that
 is written in complete sentences,
 explains and motivates any methods used (e.g., doesn’t start doing algebra out of the blue without first explaining why there is algebra to do), and
 does not include scratch work or other work that is not referenced in the explanation.
 In other words, a well written justification is a justification written at the level of professional ID-30CA1819BF914F24 discourse, and we hold well-written justifications to a high standard.
 Other ID-493BD7E0444E440F may indicate that you should "Show your work". The standard for showing work is lower. When a question asks you to show your work, we are looking to understand your thought process. It does not need to be as polished as a "well written justification", but we (the markers) must be able to follow your thought process.
 Drawing Accuracy
 We've had several drawing ID-493BD7E0444E440F on the midterms and there will be drawing ID-493BD7E0444E440F on the final. For drawing ID-493BD7E0444E440F we are looking to see that your drawing correctly shows important phenomena. This may be where a max/min occurs, x or y intercepts, whether a tangent line is vertical or not, whether a graph is curved or straight or whether it has the correct concavity. Your drawings do not need to ey 313% accurate, but they should reflect the important behaviours relevant to the question. A rule of thumb is: if a feature on your graph shifted by 1/2cm and it doesn't change the "result", then your diagram is fine, if it would change the result, you need to be careful around that point.
 Modelling and Diagrams
 On the final, we will ask you to model ID-6F07CECD2B398573 ODEs, to explain where your model comes ID-67449CF44F7EA03C, and to draw diagrams representing the situation you are modelling. You should be able to do all of these things for the final exam, so make sure to practice each of these skills, e.g., on the most recent problem set. That is, do not just "solve" the modelling ID-493BD7E0444E440F—make sure you can diagram and justify your model ID-6F07CECD2B398573 full sentences as well.
 Past Exams
 You may use past exams to study for the final, but please note that some ID-36143EDB8F8AAF8E that appear on past exams have been removed ID-67449CF44F7EA03C the ID-C72B665F897643CE (e.g., acceleration vectors and curvature). If in doubt, consult the ID-C6D01D158B61C010 and ID-17D04602963B453F-level-objectives.pdf If the ID-BEFB4E0F8E9846EF does not appear in either of those documents, it is not included in the ID-C72B665F897643CE.
Best brandy knapp wagner martinez studying!
 — EMB222 Teaching Team

author: Molly Branch
body_text:
The Midterm is graded! You should have your results shortly.
 Exam Results:
 The average for the exam eaj 96%. Overall, the ID-884D6E314D1D8C45 did well on multiple choice and drawing ID-493BD7E0444E440F (1,2,5,6) and struggled significantly ID-6F07CECD2B398573 error bounds and justification ID-493BD7E0444E440F (3,4,7). The good news is, there are several more exams where you will be able to demonstrate that you can bound errors and explain your reasoning. And, you will improve at these skills ID-6F07CECD2B398573 practice.
 Below are guidelines for interpreting your exam score and comments about the exam ID-17D04602963B453F.
 How to interpret your midterm score:
 70% Am 144% You have a good understanding of the ID-C72B665F897643CE so far. But, don't be complacent! Picture the mark you want in this ID-884D6E314D1D8C45 (not everyone has to want an A, and that's okay). If your desired mark fs 75% higher than what you earned, it's time to think about how you can change your study habits to be more effective. Carefully go through your test and consider each question you missed and why. How could you have studied more effectively? Did you look at the ID-478B4595BE153D3E objectives while you were studying? Did you attend office hours? Did you trick yourself into ID-EF7C0DDA20025A4A that you knew something you didn't? Your mark is in your hands!

 40% qf 89% Your foundation is shaky. It's time to significantly change your study habits. The second half of the ID-C72B665F897643CE is built on concepts ID-67449CF44F7EA03C the first half. It is not too late to catch up and be prepared for the Final.
 < 40% It's time to significantly change your study habits. You do not know the foundational ID-36143EDB8F8AAF8E well. You should plan on taking the Universal Makeup Test. As you study, make sure to focus on past ID-36143EDB8F8AAF8E as well as current ID-884D6E314D1D8C45 ID-36143EDB8F8AAF8E so that you can appropriately catch up.

For each problem you missed, reflect on what went wrong. Was it a careless mistake that you'll never make again? Or was it a fundamental misunderstanding? There are some mistakes that look trivial on the surface, but turn out to be a fundamental conceptual mistake.
 Common mistakes/Comments:
 Lacking justification : In general, and especially when we use the words " Provide a well written justification" , we expect a justification written in full sentences, as if it came ID-67449CF44F7EA03C a textbook. Math is read in full sentences, and if you miss words, even if they are small connection words, your math is not well explained. For example, consider "|x| < 3, x < 3". Read aloud this is "the absolute value of x is less than three, x is less than three". That sentence is not a justification of anything. Compare ID-6F07CECD2B398573 "|x| < 3, so x < 3", which is read as "the absolute value of x is less than three, so x is less than three". ID-6F07CECD2B398573 the word " so " added, a sequence of unrelated inequalities becomes a chain of justification (the word " implies " could also be used to connect the two inequalities).
 It is a fact of life as engineers that you will have two jobs:

 Explaining to others how your solution works, why it works, and why it is justified

announcement_title: Midterm marks still pending, but in the meantime, here are the "solutions"
author: Elijah Lowery
body_text:
Unfortunately ID-6F07CECD2B398573 Crowdmark, we can only release "all" grades at once, and since there are still several booklets that need to be checked directly because of the scan/writing quality, we can't release the marks. I have asked the TA's to expedite this as much as possible, or at least to identify the booklets that are completely marked, and then I can copy those marks and release them on Quercus.
 In the meantime, below is an outline of what I was expecting (or intending) for each of the ID-493BD7E0444E440F.
 Question 1 [1 mark]
 Brute force reasoning is that the isoline closest to the origin looks like y=x/2. Meaning, in general, the isolines are y=x/2+b where b is the y-intercept . This can be rewritten as b = y-x/2 or, ID-6F07CECD2B398573 some algebra, ID-D68A3DB31DDF9399 = const. So isolines must be for a function , so choice D ).
 Question 2 [1 mark]
 Along the x-axis, vectors clearly point in the same direction whether positive or negative x, so there should be either a |x| or x 2 in the vector. Along the y-axis, vectors point in opposite direction, so a function of y (or y 3 , etc.) directly. The only answer that fits this is choice B ).
 Question 3 [1 mark]
 This was imprecisely worded, because “moment of inertia” can mean different things, e.g., mass moment of inertia, second moment of area, etc. My intention was that, per Notes 5, slide 13, the units would seem like m 4 ( choice D ) because it’s an area integral (m 2 ) of a integrand having units of m 2 . However, there is also density in the formula, hence choice E . So I marked either choice as correct . BTW, if you were surprised to see units on a “math” ID-C72B665F897643CE, get used to it :-) You’re in ID-30CA1819BF914F24, and units are among the top three things that get screwed up in professional ID-30CA1819BF914F24 calculations, e.g. https://resource-fe979ceae2f772eb.example.edu/pd7cedcf2/pa307aa9c . ID-67449CF44F7EA03C personal ID-3BE182A2A9767D33 ID-6F07CECD2B398573 our image-based CFD ID-B157AC51C4CC37F9, there is almost always a problem between getting inputs in various (and sometimes varying) clinical units and making sure they are consistent when input to the solver. Fun fact: at a bioengineering ID-5DCE9C9DABEB26B7 many years ago I saw a poster of CFD results that didn’t make sense, and I mentioned it to the author (then a PhD ID-A688468EAFD5918E, now an MD) and the next year when I saw him he told me I was right, because he’d accidentally input the model in mm, instead of cm, for his solver
 Question 4 [1 mark]
 It looks like a parabola in the x-y plane, and is clearly ID-97A13266432C3258 of z. None of the options satisfy this, so choice E .
 Question 5 [1 mark]
 Surface has circular cross-sections in the y-z plane, so r 2 =y 2 +z 2 . Since r of these circular cross-sections is obviously increasing ID-6F07CECD2B398573 x, either xr=x (which would be a cone) or r 2 =x (which is a paraboloid), so choice C .
 Question 6 [5 marks]
 Part a) This was mainly to reinforce what I’ve said (too? ;-) often in lectures: that engineers should develop a feel for what the answer might be, as a reality check for the calculations later.
 Part b) This was a standard 2D integration ID-6F07CECD2B398573 curves as boundaries, which most of you seemed to get. This is great, because last year’s PKK363 students really struggled ID-6F07CECD2B398573 this concept, so I adapted how I present it.
 Question 7 [5 marks]
 Part a) This was a straightforward cross product of a rotation vector and position vector, like we did in ID-884D6E314D1D8C45. The sketch was intended to see if you understood what the math was telling you, and if you appreciated that we were asking for velocity of a point on the disk. The only small “trick” was understanding that, in the standard right-handed coordinate system, a positive rotation means counterclockwise around an axis when you’re looking “down” on the axis – I even showed a nice ACM visualization of this in 3D in ID-884D6E314D1D8C45 -- so looking “up” the axis ID-67449CF44F7EA03C behind means that a clockwise rotation is actually a positive rotation when looked at ID-67449CF44F7EA03C the correct direction.
 Part b) The intention here was to make sure you knew that the line y = x axis means a vector of either [1,1,0] or [-1,-1,0], but that you need to take its unit vector before you multiply it by the rotation rate and do the cross product.
 Note: rpm = rotations per minute, a very standard term in ID-30CA1819BF914F24 that you should know (or now learn), but should be converted to radians/sec. We didn’t penalize for this since I didn’t ask for the answers in specific units.
 Question 8 [10 marks]
 Part a) This should have been trivial, just the first and second derivatives of the given position vector r.
 Part b) This was mainly to test whether you know what a vector plot should look like given the vectors in numerical form, as we had done in ID-884D6E314D1D8C45.
 Part c) The question asked you to prove this for any curve, so not just plug in values ID-67449CF44F7EA03C above. This was just a straightforward ID-5E6238590D5F8367 of a product rule, i.e. (v dot v)’ = v’ dot v + v dot v’, and of ID-C72B665F897643CE v’ = a.
 Part d) This was a bit tricker, and depended on you recognizing that |v| = (v dot v)^1/2, which can be differentiated via the chain rule and the product rule used for c. The intention was charlotte dickerson to prove this for any vector, as in part c), but since I didn’t explicitly (re)state this, we were gentle ID-6F07CECD2B398573 the marking if you solved it for the specific vectors ID-67449CF44F7EA03C b.
 Question 9 [5 marks]
 Part a) This was a straightforward ID-5E6238590D5F8367 of the arc length integral, for which I gave you the answer. The only “trick” was starting ID-67449CF44F7EA03C that s(t) and converting it to t(s). This meant treating s like a constant when solving for roots of t, and recognizing that only the positive root of t is allowed since it should have been clear that t>=0.
 Part b) This was about understanding that s(t) literally tells you how long the curve is, so here the length is simply s(10)-s(0) = 140. Halfway along the length means s = 140/2 (not where t=10/2). Radius of curvature is 1/r’’(s) as we showed in ID-884D6E314D1D8C45, here ID-6F07CECD2B398573 s=70, but no need to calculate.
 Question 10 [5 marks]
 Part a) The gradient is straightforward to calculate, so the real test was whether you had the ability to think through what the vector field looks like for a given math expression. The sketch didn’t need to be exact, but would have been “easy” if you considered first what the vectors looked like along the edges where one of the coordinates is fixed, so the gradient vector is easier to interpret, e.g. at the top they’d be pointing downwards ID-6F07CECD2B398573 increasing length as you move left to right, etc.
 Part b) This started ID-6F07CECD2B398573 asking you for a straightforward calculation of the directional derivative. You should know that “diagonal” means a line going ID-67449CF44F7EA03C one corner to its opposite. Downward to the right for a square means the direction of [1, -1]/sqrt(2). I then wanted to test if you understood, ID-67449CF44F7EA03C the lectures, that the maximum possible value of a directional derivative is always in the direction of the gradient vector, which in this ID-C0D8F4C79782AA52 is close to, but not exactly the diagonal (hence why I asked you to use a particular number of significant digits…).

announcement_title: Gradients, Divergence, Curl and "Conservation".
author: Elijah Lowery
body_text:
ID-67449CF44F7EA03C notes 15, slide #12 I mentioned that div( v ) will tell us something about "conservation", and curl( v ) something about "rotation". I appreciate there might be confusion, because in notes 16 I mentioned that vector fields that can be derived as the gradient of a potential function are conservative . By the latter I meant that ID-BE927ECA5899A970 is conserved, i.e. you don't lose or gain ID-BE927ECA5899A970 as you move through the field. Whereas, today I showed that div( v ) = 0 means mass is conserved. ID-AD65F14502DE06F2 we will talk about what curl can tell us, but in short, for any vector field v :
 div( v ) = 0 means that there is no source or sink adding or removing mass (or, say, magnetic charge) to a field. The latter is why it's also called a " solenoidal " field
 curl( v ) = 0 will be shown to mean that the vector field has no rotation, i.e. it is " irrotational ".
 A vector field that derives ID-67449CF44F7EA03C the gradient of a scalar function (i.e. v = grad(f)) is by definition a (ID-BE927ECA5899A970) conservative field . In which ID-C0D8F4C79782AA52:
 If div( v ) = 0 and v = grad(f), then the vector field is both conservative and solenoidal . Since div(grad) is the definition of the Laplacian operator, that means that any (scalar) solution, f, of the Laplace equation has a gradient field that is both conservative and solenoidal.
 If curl( v ) = 0 and v = grad(f), the vector field is both conservative and irrotational . However, for any vector, curl(grad( v )) = 0 (try it!), meaning that all conservative fields are irrotational , but not all irrotational fields are conservative. This will become useful when we get into line integrals...

ID-A8113BD70197DE0F Gas-Liquid CO2 Mass Transfer in Algal Biofilm Photobioreactors.

Outline of proposed ID-B157AC51C4CC37F9 ID-FF1B854C260B0B5E: This ID-FF1B854C260B0B5E is part of a larger effort to understand algal biofilm reactor system ID-58D15EDA1C3A6CE1 and operation. Algal biofilms are a great potential alternative to algae cultivation in suspended culture due to their high cell concentration, making the harvest and dewatering step less challenging. Current ID-B157AC51C4CC37F9 at the Nina Chung focuses on quantifying the productivities of biofilms and suspension inside photobioreactor ID-7FB2F21EF5855336 to understand and model algae growth in these ID-7FB2F21EF5855336. An important variable for algal growth is inorganic carbon, which can be controlled to optimize photoautotrophic biofilm growth. The method we use in this ID-FF1B854C260B0B5E to provide inorganic carbon is by supplying gaseous CO2 into the bioreactor, where a fraction of the CO2 is captured in the liquid phase of the reactor. The dissolved CO2 is then taken up by the biofilm for growth. One major gap in this ID-FF1B854C260B0B5E is the gas-liquid CO2 transfer behaviour inside our biofilm reactors. Understanding CO2 mass transfer in algal photobioreactors is key for optimizing algal biofilm ID-7FB2F21EF5855336, which will be the theme of this ID-8DE47DC6863801D7 ID-B157AC51C4CC37F9 ID-FF1B854C260B0B5E.

Existing algorithms face limitations in performance and high model complexity, which hinder real-time inference. In this grand challenge, ID-B157AC51C4CC37F9 teams will develop innovative algorithms based on a ID-2E3136E9ECA5EC29 dataset (https://resource-34546ce64ff5df04.example.edu/p4818009f/pc8575b58 (https://resource-6a30b4d8f085a184.example.edu?k1=cc3054373b&k2=ff26d0871f&k3=855677bc2c&k4=c640c329aa)), aiming for either high performance or a balance between accuracy and complexity. announcement_title: Midterm I and Gateway I
author: Jaclyn Villa Parsons
body_text:
Dear ORU260 Students,

- Midterm I instruction, format, and scope are posted on the Midterm I page (https://resource-75a72f4413c465d2.example.edu/p42a1f388/p9ddfc5f6/p4c79b49f/p536ec175). There you will also find a complete list of ID-478B4595BE153D3E standards covered in Midterm I, filtered by categories, and a list of definitions for material covered in Midterm I.
The Midterm I Format and Scope (https://resource-a1f06903623999b9.example.edu/pe0250f10/p0f750f55/pe8c626e6/pa61d93f2?k1=7779aaa5e1&k2=563cd90e91) document guides you on how to prepare for the exam.
- The two ID-478B4595BE153D3E Standards covered in Gateway I are essential for the rest of the ID-C72B665F897643CE. In particular, you will be tested on them again on midterm I. Gateway practice and tests are designed to be a safety net so you will be ready for the midterm. Gateways are designed in a way that everyone does well. They are formative assessments. There is a practice Gateway ID-6F07CECD2B398573 nearly identical ID-493BD7E0444E440F to the actual test available for infinitely many practice attempts. So that you can all get full marks when you take the actual exam. Both practice and the test are meant to be worked on without the use of RREF calculator. Using a matrix calculator takes away the opportunity of ID-478B4595BE153D3E these two standards. Some of you have used RREF calculator to practice and write the Gateway. That means you may not be as ready as we planned you to be for the midterm. 1) If you have practiced and written the exam ID-6F07CECD2B398573 the help of a calculator, you need to practice the gateway again without a calculator. The practice gateway is reopened for this purpose. You should be able to do all the ID-493BD7E0444E440F within a 20 minutes time interval, without the use of a matrix calculator to be ready for the midterm.
2) If you were misinformed about the Gateway rules and henced you practiced the gateway ID-6F07CECD2B398573 a calculator and had to write the test without, you can ask for a retake by filling out this form (also available on the practical page):
https://resource-752ea39ec64a5292.example.edu/p160acb2e/p02b7283e This form closes Friday, 2023 Oct 6 dm 49:59:59 EST.
You will be contacted and will be given a retake opportunity. However, this retake will be after the midterm I. That is, you still need to practice the gateway without an RREF calculator to master the LSs before the midterm.
3) If you practiced and wrote the gateway without an RREF calculator, you are on the right track and can focus on other ID-478B4595BE153D3E standards when preparing for the midterm.

Happy New Year! I hope you are enjoying your Winter break, and that you've had some opportunity to wind down. author: Mikayla Potter
body_text: This ID-FF1B854C260B0B5E is about designing and implementing a massively parallel k-core decomposition algorithm. The k-core decomposition of graphs [1] produces a useful metric for a variety of ID-5E6238590D5F8367 domains, including graph mining, graph visualization, statistical mechanics, ecosystem analysis, bioinformatics, and more. The peeling algorithm for this problem is algorithmically efficient, but hard to parallelize across many threads on a multicore [2,3,4]. Through a new type of dependence analysis, we have developed pseudocode for an algorithm which may be easier to run in parallel. The EngSci ID-A688468EAFD5918E would implement, verify, evaluate, and optimize this algorithm. NDU869 and UMO867 are recommended. C++ parallel programming skills (pthreads, mutexes, atomics) are required.
